name: Development
one_liner: Three practices: continuous integration, evolutionary design and test-driven development.
purpose: The core of PM²-Agile lies in developing the information systems that are part of the project's solution: designing, developing, building and testing turn specifications into something tangible. The main goal is to ensure requirements are properly designed, implemented and made available through an iterative and incremental approach, while complying with architectural, infrastructural and governance constraints. To provide the necessary agility, PM²-Agile recommends three different but complementary practices.
meta: Continuous Integration, Evolutionary Design, Test-Driven Development

fields.what: Designing, developing, building and testing turn specifications into something tangible and allow the system to take shape.
fields.pollux: The portal itself, built by Lamarr, Babbage and Eiffel.

fields.what: Ensure requirements are properly designed, implemented and made available through an iterative and incremental approach.
fields.pollux: Delivered across four releases rather than one 2029 handover.

fields.what: Requirements must comply with architectural, infrastructural and governance constraints and deliver the value the business stakeholders expect.
fields.pollux: Hosting, data protection and ESM standards bind every story.

fields.what: Team members integrate their work frequently, at least daily, so integration issues are found and resolved earlier.
fields.pollux: In-house and seconded members integrate into the same mainline daily.

fields.what: The effort required to integrate a system increases exponentially with time, so frequent integration reduces the overall effort.
fields.pollux: Prevents a merge crisis before each quarterly release.

fields.what: After making changes in their validated workspaces, developers perform unit tests before making the changes available to the team.
fields.pollux: Nothing reaches the team untested, whoever employs the developer.

fields.what: Changes from all developers are merged in an integration workspace and tested frequently — at least daily, ideally on every change set.
fields.pollux: Keeps Eiffel's contract work and in-house work provably compatible.

fields.what: A higher-quality product and more predictable delivery schedules and activities, because problems are corrected while the change is fresh.
fields.pollux: Supports honest fortnightly reporting rather than late surprises.

fields.what: Based on the assumption that design evolves over time; it minimises documentation while still guiding and communicating design decisions.
fields.pollux: The data model grows with each release instead of being fixed upfront.

fields.what: During each round developers add, refine and refactor the solution rather than completing a design before implementation.
fields.pollux: Babbage's engine is refined every iteration, not designed once.

fields.what: Understand requirements, identify design elements, determine collaboration, refine decisions, design internals, communicate, understand the architecture, evaluate.
fields.pollux: Followed inside the iteration, not as a separate design phase.

fields.what: An approach where test cases are created before the actual code, and the code must pass those tests to be considered acceptable.
fields.pollux: Exposure calculations are specified as tests before they are coded.

fields.what: Reduces delivery time by decreasing time to integrate and stabilise builds, and improves productivity by fixing errors close to their introduction.
fields.pollux: Keeps the two-week iteration from ending in a stabilisation scramble.

fields.what: Increases overall quality by guaranteeing new code has been tested and existing code regression-tested prior to check-in.
fields.pollux: Protects Release 1 behaviour while Release 2 work continues.

fields.what: TDD changes the way developers think: developer tests are not an afterthought but part of the everyday way of building software.
fields.pollux: Eiffel's precision about 'done' extends to how tests get written.

traps: Continuous Integration means integrating at least daily, ideally on every change set.
TDD writes the test first, and the code must pass it to be acceptable.
Evolutionary Design minimises documentation but still communicates design decisions.
The three practices are complementary — none of them replaces the others.
Integration effort grows exponentially with delay; that is why daily matters.
